RegiÃ³n de Arica y Parinacota stands under Chile's national framework. Legal gender recognition has operated under Gender Identity Law 21,120 since 27 December 2019, allowing adults to change registered name and sex on request to the Civil Registry without therapy or surgery, with family-court proceedings for those aged 14 to 18. The 2012 Zamudio Law prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, was extended to gender expression in 2018, and treats hate-crime motivation as an aggravating criminal circumstance. Same-sex marriage and joint adoption have been legal since March 2022, civil unions since 2015, and birth certificates offer a third sex option for intersex children.

Protection for trans women under Chile's strongest gendered-violence offence is contested in the north. The Court of Appeals of Iquique annulled the entire trial over the killing of a transgender woman, holding that the femicide offence protects only "a person biologically female" and that the conviction could not stand as framed. The ruling was issued in TarapacÃ¡, the region adjoining Arica y Parinacota, and establishes that in this northern judicial area the country's femicide protection does not extend to trans women.

Complaint volumes in the region are low in national terms. Movilh's XXIII Annual Human-Rights Report on Sexual and Gender Diversity, covering 2024 and published in March 2025, recorded 2,847 cases nationally, an increase of 78.7 per cent, with Arica y Parinacota holding a 0.84 per cent share, among the lowest of any region. Increases occurred in 11 of Chile's 16 regions. In regions with shares this small, a single case can dominate the rate, so the regional figure is a weak indicator of underlying incidence.

The region's earlier trajectory ran against the national trend. Movilh's report covering 2021, published April 2022, showed homophobia and transphobia complaints and cases falling 12 per cent across Chile, the first drop in eight years, which the report tied to the visibility won by the sexual-diversity movement in the year equal marriage was approved. In five regions the figures rose, and Arica y Parinacota was one of them, with reports climbing by around 300 per cent against 2020.

A local channel for complaints exists within the region. On 14 November 2017 FundaciÃ³n Iguales announced that Arica had become the fourth territory where it provides free legal aid for discrimination cases based on sexual orientation or gender identity, through a collaboration agreement with pro-bono lawyer Piera Balbontin Nef covering Arica's jurisdiction. The foundation's legal director stated that discrimination is greater in regions far from the capital, which is why local legal support matters.

Northern courts have produced a finding materially worse for trans women than the national statutory position. The Iquique appellate ruling, delivered in TarapacÃ¡, means that a trans woman killed in this part of the country may not be covered by the femicide offence as the Court of Appeals read it, while the same killing would ordinarily attract that charge elsewhere in Chile. TarapacÃ¡ and Arica y Parinacota are grouped together as worse than the national position on shared judicial geography.

Regional complaint statistics carry a volatility problem. Arica y Parinacota's 0.84 per cent national share of 2,847 cases in 2024 is small enough that the region's rate moves sharply on very few reports, and the roughly 300 per cent rise recorded for 2021 should be read against a national decline of 12 per cent in the same year rather than as a standalone measure of conditions.

Restrictive proposals remain active at national level but are non-binding. On 15 May 2025 the Chamber of Deputies approved the CEI 57 commission report by 56 votes to 30 with 6 abstentions, a non-binding recommendation to eliminate the Gender Identity Support Program, restrict minors' progressive autonomy, ban hormonal treatment for minors and repeal the circular protecting gender identity in schools. No source in this inventory records implementation of those recommendations.
